subject: Mathematics: analysis and approaches

objectives.name: Choose and use the mathematical facts and methods you need, including in unfamiliar settings.
Solve abstract and practical problems with suitable mathematical models, results and techniques.
Turn a situation into mathematics, explain what your result means, and present your working with clear diagrams and notation.
Use suitable technology accurately to investigate ideas and solve problems.
Justify your conclusions through precise statements, logical steps and algebraic reasoning.
Investigate unfamiliar problems: organize evidence, propose a conjecture, test it and assess your conclusion.

components.name: Mathematical exploration (SL)

criteria.name: Presentation
criteria.guidance: How the exploration is organised and whether it coheres.

criteria.name: Mathematical communication
criteria.guidance: Whether the notation, terminology and representation suit the mathematics.

criteria.name: Personal engagement
criteria.guidance: Evidence of engaging with the mathematics itself, not enthusiasm for the topic.

criteria.name: Reflection
criteria.guidance: Reviewing and evaluating the exploration, not describing what was done.

criteria.name: Use of mathematics
criteria.guidance: Mathematics at the right level, correct, and visibly understood.

components.criteriaSource: Albus IB knowledge base 7.4 [OFFICIAL] — Mathematics guides, first assessment 2021

notes: No word limit; 12 to 20 pages recommended.
HL expects greater sophistication and rigour in Use of mathematics.
Cite at the point of use; a bibliography alone can become a misconduct finding.

Figures taken from the Albus IB knowledge base v1.0 (compiled August 2026), which paraphrases the official IB subject guides rather than reproducing them. Verify against the current guide before quoting marks to a student.

The two independently hosted IB briefs agree on five syllabus topic headings and six subject-wide objectives, common to AA and AI at SL and HL. These are the 2021 courses, not the separately published 2029 replacements. The exploration is an assessment activity, not a sixth topic.

Objective descriptions are Albus’s own second-person paraphrases. The matching AA guide numbers the common objectives 1–6; the briefs explicitly confirm the same objectives for AI. Per-paper ranges in that guide are not whole-subject weights, so weightingMin/Max remain null.
